title: Arista (ANET) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
transcript:
Record growth and a raised 2027 outlook drove a strong quarter.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

TAKEAWAYS

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email[email protected]

RISKS

SUMMARY

Arista Networks, Inc.(ANET+5.85%)reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, marking the highest year-over-year growth rate in its history as a public company. Management attributed this performance to accelerated demand for AI networking fabrics and steady enterprise adoption of campus and data center solutions. The company introduced its initial 2027 financial outlook, projecting revenue to reach approximately $18.5 billion as AI-related infrastructure deployments expand. Strategic initiatives focus on transitioning from compute-centric vertical stacks to network-centric architectures that support heterogeneous accelerators and open Ethernet standards.

Operator:Welcome to the Third Quarter 2026 Arista Networks Financial Results Earnings Conference Call.[Operator Instructions]As a reminder, this conference is being recorded and will be available for replay from the Investor Relations section on the Arista website following this call. Mr. Rudolph Araujo, Arista's Head of Investor Advocacy, you may begin.

Rudolph Araujo:Thank you, Regina. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. With me on today's call are Jayshree Ullal, Arista Networks' Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer; and Chantelle Breithaupt, Arista's Chief Financial Officer. This afternoon, Arista Networks issued a press release announcing its fiscal third quarter results for the period ending September 30, 2026. If you want a copy of this release, you can find it on our website. During the course of this conference call, Arista Networks management will make forward-looking statements, including those relating to our financial outlook for the fourth quarter of the 2026 fiscal year, longer-term business model and financial outlook for 2027 and beyond.

Our total addressable market and strategy for accessing those market opportunities across AI, campus, data center and other segments, inventory levels and management, lead times, purchase commitments, component supply and product innovation, which are subject to the risks and uncertainties that we discuss in detail in our documents filed with the SEC, specifically in our most recent Form 10-Q and Form 10-K and which could cause actual results to differ materially from those anticipated by these statements. These forward-looking statements apply as of today, and you should not rely on them as representing our views in the future. We undertake no obligation to update these statements after this call.

This analysis of our Q3 results and our guidance for Q4 2026 and FY 2027 is based on non-GAAP financial measures and excludes stock-based compensation expense, intangible asset amortization and other nonrecurring items as well as the income tax effect of these non-GAAP exclusions, including the recognition of direct access tax benefits associated with stock-based awards. A full reconciliation of our selected GAAP to non-GAAP historical results is provided in our earnings release. A reconciliation of our FY '27 non-GAAP guidance to the most directly comparable GAAP measures is not available without unreasonable effort. With that, I will turn the call over to Jayshree.

Jayshree Ullal:Thank you, Rudy, and welcome, everyone, to our third quarter 2026 earnings call. Arista just delivered a standout quarter of $3.66 billion in revenue, which is translating to our annual growth of 58.5%. This marks our largest ever year-over-year revenue growth in the history of being a public company. Before we dive into the financial specifics, I would like to emphasize our rapid Arista 2.0 success, a strategy we embarked upon just 3 years ago. It has generated meaningful customer outcomes to become the central network nervous system for us. In the 2000 era, the industry had accepted a status quo, plagued by fragile, overly complex, disparate and vulnerable operating systems.

Arista pioneered the universal cloud network and the AI leaf-spine architecture based upon our rock-solid, high-quality foundation of our differentiated EOS. That one network operating system with a publish-subscribe state and data-driven foundation has governed us with 5 As: agile security, automation, availability, analytics, and AI principles. By extending our single EOS operating system from the data center all the way from the universal spine to many forms of edge leaf functions, we deliver structural and secure network harmony. Our Arista 2.0 transformation from data centers to centers of data can be characterized as the age of network intelligence, learning from vast repositories of streamed data.

It has driven our strategy across locations, be it client to branch, to campus, to data, to cloud and AI centers for our customers. Based on our network data lake architecture, we offer our customers automated and conversational troubleshooting agentic companions. Devoid of manual hunting through text-heavy logs, our systems proactively begin identifying and isolating issues for network workloads, workflows and work streams. In 2026, the network-centric acceleration is well underway. Our customers have increasingly coalesced the back end and the front end of AI and data centers. Arista has long championed standards-based Ethernet. Customers have welcomed our open approach to modernizing cloud, campus, data centers, WAN centers and now AI centers with a lower total cost of ownership.

Recently, we were recognized with the leader status from Forrester for the highest strength of innovation and data center portfolio. We were also recognized by Gartner Magic Quadrant Leadership for campus, wired and wireless, and data center segments. As agentic AI models increase in parallelism, compute diversity and density, we have the choice of many more training and inference accelerators. The industry, we believe, is shifting from compute-centric vertical stack to a holistic network-centric approach. Arista is committed to unleashing and breaking down the barriers between compute and networking. Arista customers can now construct an open network platform capable of handling heterogeneous models and diverse accelerators at scale.

Our Etherlink portfolio of at least 25 switches for scale-up, scale-out and scale-across is optimally designed to improve XPU utilization, job completion time and token latency for these intense training and inference workloads. In October of 2026, at the Open Compute Project conference, Arista showcased our rack scale-up designs, partnering closely with several AI accelerators infused with our Arista network diagnostics layer. Based on ESUN, Ethernet for scale-up, rack options, these include orthogonal designs, cable-intensive backplanes and heterogeneous cross-rack designs co-designed with many of our partners, including Arm, Microsoft Maia, AMD's Helios, Qualcomm, Meta's MTIA and many more ahead.

We expect scale-up trials to begin in 2027, driving Ethernet to larger radix of 126 to 144 within a rack and across 1,000 across racks, with production expected for scale-up in 2028. We are witnessing the migration from highly centralized training compute to disaggregated and distributed inference, prefill and decode, demanding much more intelligent networking and colocation of compute, storage and KV cache resources rather than simply focusing on raw feeds and speeds and flops of compute. A well-designed network is becoming a foundational cornerstone for optimal token efficiency.

Arista's decades of EOS engineering in both multiplanar and distributed models routing at scale, be it ARP, address resolution protocols, or FIB tables, forwarding information base, or access list with rapid reconvergence comes to the rescue. Our Etherlink products are inherently designed to actively understand parameters at a deep level, including latency and bandwidth profiles of multitenancy to intelligently steer workloads for optimal placement between local and remote domains. The need for visibility into ports, packet queues, flows, buffer utilization and path latency across the entire scale-out and scale-across fabric validates [ real-time ] AI system level performance to avoid idling of precious compute cycles.

It assures immediate and network-wide insight to the root cause as well as rapid recovery of the AI system with smart system upgrades across millions of accelerators. When we initially began this transformational AI journey, we spoke about 4 or 5 AI customers with approximately 50,000 to 100,000 NVIDIA GPUs. And in fact, we were largely staring at a proprietary network cycle such as InfiniBand. In 2026, we are in a super cycle of AI, having already surpassed 100 Etherlink customers. By the end of '27, we are forecasting greater than 10 gigawatts of deployment across 10 or more different types of compute accelerators. What a stark inflection in just 3 years.

Central to this AI super cycle is also the expansion of Arista AVA, our Autonomous Virtual Assist, to support efficient AI in the enterprise. By providing that open programmable interface within EOS and utilizing the Model Context Protocol, MCP, AVA allows emerging AI agents to reason, to interact with the network stack and perform advanced multidomain event correlation across the entire enterprise. With exponential rise of generative AI attacks and the ever-increasing cyber threats, securing the network is key and integral and our responsibility. I would like to invite Ken Duda, our Founder, President and CTO, to shed some light on this problem. Ken?

Kenneth Duda:Thanks, Jayshree. It's hard to overstate the impact of AI on networking. First, the good news, AVA, which is Arista's Autonomous Virtual Assistant, fueled by real-time data, AVA is incredibly powerful. It seamlessly navigates networking and security infrastructure from campus to WAN, to data center, to cloud, continuously monitoring and troubleshooting, isolating root causes without manual labor-intensive tasks. Having seen what AVA can do, I can't imagine managing my own infrastructure without it, and I expect many of our customers will feel the same way. The bad news, of course, is the massive challenge AI poses for us and our customers by discovering and exploiting security vulnerabilities. This threat landscape demands secure and robust networking.

Over the past few months, we've been collaborating with Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and many others to integrate new AI-enabled security capabilities from frontier models into our existing software security pipeline. We are being invited early as a key infrastructure provider into partnerships like Project Glasswing, building AI-driven vulnerability discovery and assessment into our established security vulnerability management process. True network security has become a must-have, not a nice-to-have, and Arista's EOS operating system is the ideal architectural foundation based on 4 key principles. First, a single high-quality operating system.

Arista has maintained one of the lowest CVE counts, less than 100 in the industry over the last 2 decades, while others are rising exponentially due in part to the simple fact that multiple networking operating systems tend to have more vulnerabilities than just one. Second, limiting vulnerability impact through process isolation. EOS keeps each software agent, management plane or control plane, architecturally separate from each other and also from hardware forwarding, so traffic keeps moving even if there is a defect in one component. EOS's state-sharing architecture also resists lateral movement. So a defect in one component typically cannot be exploited to attack other agents within the switch. Third, we provide a seamless upgrade process.

Process isolation also means that we can ship a targeted fix to the affected component and install the fix without a maintenance window or network disruption. And fourth, delivering a compliance dashboard to stay current. When a security advisory lands, Arista CloudVision brings real-time visibility that turns a stressful advisory day into a manageable one. In addition to providing secure switches, we also provide Zero Trust Networking, or ZTN technology, to help our customers build secure infrastructure. I'd especially like to highlight Macro Segmentation Services, or MSS, a ZTN feature allowing for dynamic security enforcement, preventing undesired interactions among users, devices and applications.

Second, we provide Network Detection and Response, or NDR services, that profile, analyze and proactively detect sophisticated security threats. And finally, once workload traffic leaves the confines of the local data center, it becomes even more vulnerable to malicious actors. So we offer protection with wire speed ubiquitous link and tunnel encryption native in every port with 0 performance degradation. I hope this was a helpful summary of how Arista is helping customers take advantage of AI while improving security to meet the new challenges. Back over to you, Jayshree.

Jayshree Ullal:Thank you, Ken. It was useful for me, too. With Arista's uncompromised ZTN approach, we can systematically address the security hazards and parabolic attacks. Our CVE count, our vulnerability count is often 10 to 50x better than alternatives. Our customer momentum this year has been significant to the enterprise in the providers across data center, campus and AI because we are addressing security proactively. I would like to invite Todd Nightingale, our President and Chief Operating Officer, to describe more about this. Over to you, Todd.

Todd Nightingale:Thanks, Jayshree. We're seeing phenomenal growth across our enterprise business, driven by customers building mission-critical networks, which benefit from Arista's industry-leading quality and reliability. As the entire industry responds to AI-powered attack exposure, customers are motivated by the fact that keeping their infrastructure current with security updates will protect, segment and defend against vulnerabilities beyond the network. Arista won a strategic deal at an Asian web services company as they shifted their focus strategically on the speed, scale and resilience in the new AI era. Reliability was the key to the engagement as their teams are frustrated by long-standing quality issues with their existing vendor.

Arista was able to demonstrate reliability and scalability while leveraging standards-based technology and a powerful EVPN-VXLAN architecture on our 100- and 400-gig platforms. This deployment will operate as the front end for their AI deployments moving forward. In the health care sector, leading hospitals are selecting Arista for strategic data center deployment. One important hospital group chose Arista following an exhaustive Zero Trust Networking evaluation. Their primary business goal was to protect sensitive patient data through advanced network segmentation while enabling seamless integration to cloud environments. Arista secured this win by delivering an automated high-performance fabric that perfectly aligned with their trust nothing, verify everything security mandate.

By centralizing routing on Arista's R3 spines, we provided a powerful streamlined layer for traffic management tailored to modern health care workloads with a robust leaf-spine topology. We deployed CloudVision-as-a-Service alongside the Arista AVD framework for cloud-based automation and deep visibility. And by integrating Arista's segmentation service, MSS, the customer can now dynamically automate the entire system. In the hospitality sector, an award-winning regional resort and casino selected Arista to modernize its expanding operations. Realizing their legacy network was a bottleneck for innovation, they architected a truly unified standards-based architecture across their data center and campus environments to support new guest experiences and rapidly scale their services.

Arista's routing and switching platforms alongside campus access switches are delivering quality and reliability key to performing in mission-critical applications like their demanding casino gaming floor network. They utilize CloudVision and AVD to automate device provisioning and gain the deep real-time visibility required to optimize network performance. In all 3 of these examples, Arista's differentiated EOS provided unmatched quality and reliability and integrated seamlessly with their overarching security ecosystem partners. Additionally, our TAC delivered the flawless experience and peace of mind to derisk these modern enterprise migrations to Arista. 2026 has really been an exciting year building momentum across our entire enterprise business around the world in data center, campus and AI build-outs. Thank you, Jayshree.

Jayshree Ullal:Thank you, Todd. Wow, that momentum is indeed unprecedented. I haven't experienced anything like this until you arrived. We are pleased with Arista's accelerated networking progress across all our sectors. Our commitment to fulfilling this accelerated demand in the second half of 2026 is really playing out well with our improved execution in supply chain, partnering closely with our vendors. I want to give a special kudos to you and your entire manufacturing team led by Eugenia for the tireless work and progress despite the widespread industry-wide supply chain constraints and shortages. With this backdrop, we are now increasing our annual guidance for the fourth time in 2026 to $13.3 billion, which represents a 48% annual growth.

At Arista, we find ourselves in a position to address this ever-increasing total accessible market, not just available market, which now stands at north of $200 billion in 2030, therefore, representing a multiyear growth opportunity for us. Our first look at 2027 guidance range puts us in the 38% to 40% range for growth annually to approximately $18.5 billion. Within this envelope, we expect our AI fabrics target to be the fastest-growing segment and to double to approximately $7 billion, while our cognitive campus represents a healthy growth of 60%, much faster than the market to approximately $2 billion in 2027. We do live in exciting times as we harness the power of cloud and AI revolution.

It has certainly surpassed my expectations as we exceeded our original $10 billion goal this year to enter revenue dollars in the teens for both 2026 and 2027. We do so in the typical Arista way, bringing our unique combination of innovations, quality, profitability, efficiency and 0 debt, making our financials very pristine. Our results would not be possible without the cohesive Aristan leadership and team, our elite customers and partners and, of course, our supportive shareholders. And with that, over to you, Chantelle, to shed more light on our impressive financials.

Chantelle Breithaupt:Thank you, Jayshree. This quarter, we delivered record high revenue growth since our IPO at 58.5%, partnered with robust operating margin above 49%. At the same time, we invested ahead of demand in R&D, inventory and supply commitments to support the AI opportunity in front of us. Congratulations to the Arista team for being named to the S&P 100 in September, a great achievement within a short time frame. Let's dive into the financial details. To start off, total revenues in Q3 were approximately $3.66 billion, up 58.5% year-over-year and above our guidance of $3.3 billion. This significant growth was driven by our continued strength in both AI and enterprise customers.

International revenues for the quarter came in at $682.5 million, or 18.6% of total revenue, down from 23% last quarter. This quarter-over-quarter change was primarily influenced by a shift in the geographic mix of sales to our large global customers. Year-over-year double-digit growth was achieved in all 3 geographic segments. The overall gross margin in Q3 was 64%, down from 65.2% in the prior year, with supply chain efficiency working to partially offset product cost inflation, and up from 63.4% in the prior quarter, driven by end customer mix. Operating expenses for the quarter were $545.3 million, or 14.9% of revenue, up from the last quarter of $411 million.

Our R&D spending came in at $408.5 million, or 11.2% of revenue, up from the last quarter at $278.1 million. Arista continues to demonstrate its commitment and focus on network innovation with additional investment in liquid cooling, high-radix switching and leading AI software. Sales and marketing expense was $110.9 million, or 3% of revenue, down slightly from 3.6% of revenue last quarter, representative of the highly efficient Arista go-to-market methodology. Our G&A costs came in at $25.9 million, or 0.7% of revenue, up slightly from $23.1 million last quarter as we continue to focus on our critical corporate systems and processes.

Our operating income for the quarter was $1.8 billion, or 49.1% of revenue, demonstrating our ability to invest in innovation while expanding profitability. Other income and expense for the quarter was a favorable $138.6 million, and our effective tax rate was 20.9%. Overall, this resulted in net income for the quarter of $1.53 billion, or 41.9% of revenue. Our diluted share number was 1.278 billion shares, resulting in a diluted earnings per share for the quarter of $1.20, up significantly with a growth of 55.8% from $0.77 in the prior year period. Now turning to the balance sheet. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities ended the quarter at approximately $14.4 billion, up from $13.3 billion at the end of Q2.

Of the $1.5 billion stock repurchase program approved in May of 2025, $817.9 million remain available for repurchase in future quarters. The actual timing and amount of future repurchases will be dependent on market and business conditions, stock price and other factors. Now turning to operating cash performance for the third quarter. We generated approximately $1.2 billion of cash from operations. This was driven by a robust earnings performance, coupled with an intentional inventory build to meet our growing customer demand. DSOs came in at 59 days, down from 68 days in Q2 due to the timing of customer shipments and invoicing. Our inventory turns dropped slightly from 1.7 in Q2 to 1.6 for the quarter.

We ended the quarter with $3.2 billion in inventory, up from $2.5 billion last quarter. Inventory level fluctuations are expected to continue as we work through the balancing of component timing and availability. This could result in quarters of elevated inventory balances affecting the timing of cash flow from operations ahead of customer deployments. Our purchase commitments at the end of the quarter were $11.4 billion, up from $9.7 billion at the end of Q2. As mentioned in prior quarters, this expected activity mostly represents purchases for chips related to new products and AI deployments. Our total deferred revenue balance was approximately $6.8 billion, down from $6.9 billion in the prior quarter.

The majority of the deferred revenue balance is product related. Our product deferred revenue decreased $86 million sequentially versus last quarter. We remain in a period of ramping our new products, winning new customers and expanding new use cases, including AI. These trends have resulted in increased customer-specific acceptance clauses and an increase in the volatility of our product deferred revenue balances. As mentioned in prior quarters, the deferred balance can move significantly on a quarterly basis, independent of underlying business drivers. Accounts payable days were 48 days, down from 57 days in Q2, reflecting the timing of inventory receipts and payments. Capital expenditures for the quarter were $100.7 million.

Our construction work to build expanded facilities in Santa Clara remains on track, and we expect construction to be completed in the coming months. As we look ahead, the momentum is strong. We are grateful to our customers and proud of our team's continuous ability to rise to meet the demands of the networking industry. For the fourth quarter, we are forecasting a range of revenue between $3.9 billion and $4 billion. This positions fiscal year 2026 revenue just over $13.3 billion at the midpoint. Our fourth quarter gross margin outlook is 63% to 64% and operating margin is between 48% and 49%.

Diluted EPS is forecasted to be between $1.26 and $1.30 with approximately 1.28 billion diluted shares, and the effective tax rate is expected to be approximately 21%. Looking further ahead to 2027, the momentum continues. For fiscal year 2027, the revenue growth outlook is between 38% and 40%, equating to approximately $18.5 billion at the midpoint. Gross margin continues to be in the range of 62% to 64% and an operating margin of approximately 49%. Our effective tax rate is expected to be approximately 21%. In closing, there is a lot to be excited about here at Arista. We will continue to be focused on our innovation, execution and delighting customers in the Arista way.

Now back to you, Rudy, for Q&A.

Rudolph Araujo:Thank you, Chantelle. We will now move to the Q&A portion of the Arista earnings call.[Operator Instructions]Regina, please take it away.

Operator:[Operator Instructions]Our first question comes from the line of Michael Ng with Goldman Sachs.

Michael Ng:I wanted to ask about your comment around the greater than 10 gigawatts of deployments across 10-plus compute accelerators for next year. Could you just talk a little bit about whether that is an industry number or an Arista-specific number in terms of those deployments? And how does the diversification of compute potentially create more opportunities for Arista networking relative to just having a handful of compute suppliers?

Jayshree Ullal:Thanks, Michael. As you know, I think much of AI, even in our world started initially being compute-centric, and we're seeing that change to network-centric. And so as part of the accelerated networking strategy, we are supporting 3 types of AI fabrics, scale-up, scale-out and scale-across. So our guess is by the end of '27, we will deploy largely in '26 and '27, is where the exponential ramp happened, across or greater than 10 gigawatts. Now some of that -- much of that gigawatt may be new. But remember, in scale-across, we can also have existing gigawatts being deployed. So we're talking about new distributed 10 gigawatts, but there may already be multiple gigawatts deployed across.

So the rationale here is while we are new to scale-up, we are touching a variety of XPUs and scale-out and scale-across, across the rack and across data centers. And we already know with our scale-across, we are touching multiple XPUs, 4 or 5 of them. With the advent of scale-up, we will add another 5 in 2027.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of Meta Marshall with Morgan Stanley.

Meta Marshall:Congrats on the quarter. I guess just, Jayshree, if you could give an update just on how you see that mix of scale-across and scale-out and scale-up just as a mix of your business. Clearly, scale-up nothing today. I think last quarter, you had said you expected 1/3 of the demand this year to be from scale-across. Just as you've continued to increase your guidance and as you look into '27, just what do you see those mixes being?

Jayshree Ullal:I think in '27 -- Meta, thank you for the kind wishes. We've been working hard for this day. The scale-up will still be in early trials. So I don't think there's a material number associated with scale-up in '27. I do think it could contribute in '28. So then that -- if scale-up is virtually 0, then we're basically left with most of the use case being scale-out and scale-across. And as you've heard us say in the past, scale-across, we think, will be at least 1/3. It will probably go higher in '27. And so the split this year is roughly 70-30.

The split next year may be -- I can't venture to guess, but I think the 70 may come down and the 30 would go up when it comes to scale-across because it's a very strong use case for us. Arista is highly differentiated with our 7800 scale-across platform. And unsurprisingly, the word scale means a lot to us there and our customers, scale for security, scale for performance, scale for reliability, and there's just no room for error when you're connecting millions of XPUs. So we feel very comfortable that these are our 2 strongest use cases. I also think it will fuel -- I mean, a lot of this is back-end AI fabric.

We will come back to revisit a question of front end as well as we move to more inference and the line between back and front becomes thinner.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of Ben Reitzes with Melius Research.

Benjamin Reitzes:Jayshree, pretty good quarter guide there. So I just want -- you've previously referred to potentially 2 10%-plus customers into the fourth quarter. Do you mind talking about whether they're landing in that range and what the use cases are for and if you're excited about those customers still and into '27?

Jayshree Ullal:Yes. Yes, yes. So I guess diversity is the name of the game and the theme today, right, Chantelle?

Chantelle Breithaupt:That's right.

Jayshree Ullal:We have diverse accelerators. We have diverse models. We want to have diverse 10% customers, too. So as we said before, our dearest ones are M&M. We fully expect our top prior 10%-plus customers to continue to be with us in '26, and we hope beyond. And we expect to add at least 1, maybe 2. And a lot of that depends on whether Todd and Eugenia can ship enough product. So we'll let them decide, and we'll give them all the way into December 31.

Todd Nightingale:We'll take every day.

Jayshree Ullal:So we're feeling pretty good about at least 3 and maybe 4.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of George Notter with Wolfe Research.

George Notter:I was just curious about the big sequential jump in R&D. It was really, really significant. I'm just wondering if that included some onetime items. Also, is this the new run rate in R&D going forward? Any perspective there would be great.

Jayshree Ullal:Okay. So over to you, Ken. Why did you spend so much money this year?

Kenneth Duda:We're building so much new stuff. The opportunity is humongous in AI, these AI accelerating systems are -- we are -- our success with the hyperscaler AI companies depends on our ability to partner. Our ability to partner is based on our understanding of each of their unique requirements and constraints. And also, there's a new technology introduction around liquid cooling. This requires major infrastructure upgrades and technology upgrades on our part. So I think that's what's really driving the expansion in spending there.

Chantelle Breithaupt:Sorry, George, just in your comment, is this new run rate, I'll still put the framework at anywhere between 9% and 11% as we work through. So some quarters like we've talked about, we'll hit this range as we have specific investments. And so I would still keep it in that 9% to 11%. More to come as we guide next year in more detail.

Jayshree Ullal:But I noticed the prototype bill was very high this quarter, Ken.

Kenneth Duda:That's right, because of all the opportunities in the hyperscaler AI space.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of Amit Daryanani with Evercore ISI.

Amit Daryanani:Congrats on a really good set of numbers over here. Jayshree, you talked initially about the industry moving towards a more network-centric architecture. As customers deploy different type of accelerators, does Arista become involved earlier in designing the overall systems rather than connecting them afterwards? And as you have to work with a more distributed disaggregated compute network, does that change your networking content per deployment? I know you talked about 10 gigawatts, I'm just sort of wondering, does the network intensity start to change as well?

And then maybe for Chantelle, as you think about this 38%, 40% guide for '27, which is extremely impressive, can you just touch on your confidence around the supply chain execution to meet this demand? What's in the bag versus what still needs to be closed?

Jayshree Ullal:Amit, this is a very good question. I think until now, we've enforced our architecture mostly on scale-out and scale-across. And a lot of that had to do with distributed power, location, moving to regional edges, a very software-defined type of network with the intensity, like I described, of package, flows, performance, predictable latency, et cetera. As we start participating with new accelerators, we get a greater chance early in the cycle to see the behavior of these accelerators. Two or 3 examples I'd like to highlight is our close work with Cerebras, our work with Microsoft and Maia.

These have been going on the last couple of years and has allowed us to tune our buffers, tune our software performance and maximize the I/O throughput, if you will. The recognition of those scale-up designs are still in the works, but they're already manifesting itself in scale-out and scale-across. So you bring up a very good point, not only in the actual work we're doing with these accelerators, but the aggregate impact it has on our network design in terms of scale, performance and reliability.

Chantelle Breithaupt:And then I think to part two of your question, Amit, and thank you for the kind words at the beginning, I think -- so I am confident in the guide, and I am confident in the supply chain. What makes me confident in the supply chain is internally, Todd and Eugenia and the team doing a fantastic job every day, being scrappy to make sure we can do what we need to do to deliver to our customers. And I also have confidence in a lot of great conversations and agreements with some of our key suppliers, and that's why you see our purchase commitments increasing because we have that confidence. So internally, externally confident.

As far as visibility, I think we have 2 quarters of visibility as we always have, and we lean into the other 2. But given our highly fungible portfolio, we're pretty clear where to make that bet. So we're pretty excited about next year.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of Tim Long with Barclays.

Timothy Long:Maybe if we could shift a little bit and talk about the campus and branch, pretty good year this year and guiding it to 60% next year. Could you talk a little bit about kind of what's enabling you to grow so much faster than the industry? And is this something that you see as a multiyear type of dynamic? Obviously, you got strength in enterprise data centers. But curious what else is helping this much higher than industry growth?

Todd Nightingale:Thanks for the question. In a lot of ways, I think the enterprise campus market is coming to us. Arista has always led the way in quality and reliability. And over the past few years, just practically every significant enterprise has shifted gears and really considered their campus networks, their branch networks mission-critical, with the highest need for reliability. This has only accelerated because of the Glasswing and Mythos effect where people are really focused deeply not only on providing the highest level of reliability, but being able to do that as they rapidly patch and adjust their infrastructure over time.

And the differentiation with EOS and the ability for Arista software to be able to do this with practically no downtime with extremely, extremely high uptime, it's highly differentiated in the market. And I really think that's the core of what's driving market share gains here.

Kenneth Duda:I think the other thing that makes this an incremental process is that campus refresh cycles are pretty long. So even customers that understand the Arista advantage may take some time to adopt us simply because of the schedule on which they depreciate and upgrade their gear. So I think we can expect this to be a multiyear cycle.

Kenneth Duda:Thanks, Jayshree. It's hard to overstate the impact of AI on networking. First, the good news, AVA, which is Arista's Autonomous Virtual Assistant, fueled by real-time data, AVA is incredibly powerful. It seamlessly navigates networking and security infrastructure from campus to WAN, to data center, to cloud, continuously monitoring and troubleshooting, isolating root causes without manual labor-intensive tasks. Having seen what AVA can do, I can't imagine managing my own infrastructure without it, and I expect many of our customers will feel the same way. The bad news, of course, is the massive challenge AI poses for us and our customers by discovering and exploiting security vulnerabilities. This threat landscape demands secure and robust networking.

Over the past few months, we've been collaborating with Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and many others to integrate new AI-enabled security capabilities from frontier models into our existing software security pipeline. We are being invited early as a key infrastructure provider into partnerships like Project Glasswing, building AI-driven vulnerability discovery and assessment into our established security vulnerability management process. True network security has become a must-have, not a nice-to-have, and Arista's EOS operating system is the ideal architectural foundation based on 4 key principles. First, a single high-quality operating system.

Arista has maintained one of the lowest CVE counts, less than 100 in the industry over the last 2 decades, while others are rising exponentially due in part to the simple fact that multiple networking operating systems tend to have more vulnerabilities than just one. Second, limiting vulnerability impact through process isolation. EOS keeps each software agent, management plane or control plane, architecturally separate from each other and also from hardware forwarding, so traffic keeps moving even if there is a defect in one component. EOS's state-sharing architecture also resists lateral movement. So a defect in one component typically cannot be exploited to attack other agents within the switch. Third, we provide a seamless upgrade process.

Process isolation also means that we can ship a targeted fix to the affected component and install the fix without a maintenance window or network disruption. And fourth, delivering a compliance dashboard to stay current. When a security advisory lands, Arista CloudVision brings real-time visibility that turns a stressful advisory day into a manageable one. In addition to providing secure switches, we also provide Zero Trust Networking, or ZTN technology, to help our customers build secure infrastructure. I'd especially like to highlight Macro Segmentation Services, or MSS, a ZTN feature allowing for dynamic security enforcement, preventing undesired interactions among users, devices and applications.

Second, we provide Network Detection and Response, or NDR services, that profile, analyze and proactively detect sophisticated security threats. And finally, once workload traffic leaves the confines of the local data center, it becomes even more vulnerable to malicious actors. So we offer protection with wire speed ubiquitous link and tunnel encryption native in every port with 0 performance degradation. I hope this was a helpful summary of how Arista is helping customers take advantage of AI while improving security to meet the new challenges. Back over to you, Jayshree.

Jayshree Ullal:Thank you, Ken. It was useful for me, too. With Arista's uncompromised ZTN approach, we can systematically address the security hazards and parabolic attacks. Our CVE count, our vulnerability count is often 10 to 50x better than alternatives. Our customer momentum this year has been significant to the enterprise in the providers across data center, campus and AI because we are addressing security proactively. I would like to invite Todd Nightingale, our President and Chief Operating Officer, to describe more about this. Over to you, Todd.

Todd Nightingale:Thanks, Jayshree. We're seeing phenomenal growth across our enterprise business, driven by customers building mission-critical networks, which benefit from Arista's industry-leading quality and reliability. As the entire industry responds to AI-powered attack exposure, customers are motivated by the fact that keeping their infrastructure current with security updates will protect, segment and defend against vulnerabilities beyond the network. Arista won a strategic deal at an Asian web services company as they shifted their focus strategically on the speed, scale and resilience in the new AI era. Reliability was the key to the engagement as their teams are frustrated by long-standing quality issues with their existing vendor.

Arista was able to demonstrate reliability and scalability while leveraging standards-based technology and a powerful EVPN-VXLAN architecture on our 100- and 400-gig platforms. This deployment will operate as the front end for their AI deployments moving forward. In the health care sector, leading hospitals are selecting Arista for strategic data center deployment. One important hospital group chose Arista following an exhaustive Zero Trust Networking evaluation. Their primary business goal was to protect sensitive patient data through advanced network segmentation while enabling seamless integration to cloud environments. Arista secured this win by delivering an automated high-performance fabric that perfectly aligned with their trust nothing, verify everything security mandate.

By centralizing routing on Arista's R3 spines, we provided a powerful streamlined layer for traffic management tailored to modern health care workloads with a robust leaf-spine topology. We deployed CloudVision-as-a-Service alongside the Arista AVD framework for cloud-based automation and deep visibility. And by integrating Arista's segmentation service, MSS, the customer can now dynamically automate the entire system. In the hospitality sector, an award-winning regional resort and casino selected Arista to modernize its expanding operations. Realizing their legacy network was a bottleneck for innovation, they architected a truly unified standards-based architecture across their data center and campus environments to support new guest experiences and rapidly scale their services.

Arista's routing and switching platforms alongside campus access switches are delivering quality and reliability key to performing in mission-critical applications like their demanding casino gaming floor network. They utilize CloudVision and AVD to automate device provisioning and gain the deep real-time visibility required to optimize network performance. In all 3 of these examples, Arista's differentiated EOS provided unmatched quality and reliability and integrated seamlessly with their overarching security ecosystem partners. Additionally, our TAC delivered the flawless experience and peace of mind to derisk these modern enterprise migrations to Arista. 2026 has really been an exciting year building momentum across our entire enterprise business around the world in data center, campus and AI build-outs. Thank you, Jayshree.

Jayshree Ullal:Thank you, Todd. Wow, that momentum is indeed unprecedented. I haven't experienced anything like this until you arrived. We are pleased with Arista's accelerated networking progress across all our sectors. Our commitment to fulfilling this accelerated demand in the second half of 2026 is really playing out well with our improved execution in supply chain, partnering closely with our vendors. I want to give a special kudos to you and your entire manufacturing team led by Eugenia for the tireless work and progress despite the widespread industry-wide supply chain constraints and shortages. With this backdrop, we are now increasing our annual guidance for the fourth time in 2026 to $13.3 billion, which represents a 48% annual growth.

At Arista, we find ourselves in a position to address this ever-increasing total accessible market, not just available market, which now stands at north of $200 billion in 2030, therefore, representing a multiyear growth opportunity for us. Our first look at 2027 guidance range puts us in the 38% to 40% range for growth annually to approximately $18.5 billion. Within this envelope, we expect our AI fabrics target to be the fastest-growing segment and to double to approximately $7 billion, while our cognitive campus represents a healthy growth of 60%, much faster than the market to approximately $2 billion in 2027. We do live in exciting times as we harness the power of cloud and AI revolution.

It has certainly surpassed my expectations as we exceeded our original $10 billion goal this year to enter revenue dollars in the teens for both 2026 and 2027. We do so in the typical Arista way, bringing our unique combination of innovations, quality, profitability, efficiency and 0 debt, making our financials very pristine. Our results would not be possible without the cohesive Aristan leadership and team, our elite customers and partners and, of course, our supportive shareholders. And with that, over to you, Chantelle, to shed more light on our impressive financials.

Chantelle Breithaupt:Thank you, Jayshree. This quarter, we delivered record high revenue growth since our IPO at 58.5%, partnered with robust operating margin above 49%. At the same time, we invested ahead of demand in R&D, inventory and supply commitments to support the AI opportunity in front of us. Congratulations to the Arista team for being named to the S&P 100 in September, a great achievement within a short time frame. Let's dive into the financial details. To start off, total revenues in Q3 were approximately $3.66 billion, up 58.5% year-over-year and above our guidance of $3.3 billion. This significant growth was driven by our continued strength in both AI and enterprise customers.

International revenues for the quarter came in at $682.5 million, or 18.6% of total revenue, down from 23% last quarter. This quarter-over-quarter change was primarily influenced by a shift in the geographic mix of sales to our large global customers. Year-over-year double-digit growth was achieved in all 3 geographic segments. The overall gross margin in Q3 was 64%, down from 65.2% in the prior year, with supply chain efficiency working to partially offset product cost inflation, and up from 63.4% in the prior quarter, driven by end customer mix. Operating expenses for the quarter were $545.3 million, or 14.9% of revenue, up from the last quarter of $411 million.

Our R&D spending came in at $408.5 million, or 11.2% of revenue, up from the last quarter at $278.1 million. Arista continues to demonstrate its commitment and focus on network innovation with additional investment in liquid cooling, high-radix switching and leading AI software. Sales and marketing expense was $110.9 million, or 3% of revenue, down slightly from 3.6% of revenue last quarter, representative of the highly efficient Arista go-to-market methodology. Our G&A costs came in at $25.9 million, or 0.7% of revenue, up slightly from $23.1 million last quarter as we continue to focus on our critical corporate systems and processes.

Our operating income for the quarter was $1.8 billion, or 49.1% of revenue, demonstrating our ability to invest in innovation while expanding profitability. Other income and expense for the quarter was a favorable $138.6 million, and our effective tax rate was 20.9%. Overall, this resulted in net income for the quarter of $1.53 billion, or 41.9% of revenue. Our diluted share number was 1.278 billion shares, resulting in a diluted earnings per share for the quarter of $1.20, up significantly with a growth of 55.8% from $0.77 in the prior year period. Now turning to the balance sheet. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities ended the quarter at approximately $14.4 billion, up from $13.3 billion at the end of Q2.

Of the $1.5 billion stock repurchase program approved in May of 2025, $817.9 million remain available for repurchase in future quarters. The actual timing and amount of future repurchases will be dependent on market and business conditions, stock price and other factors. Now turning to operating cash performance for the third quarter. We generated approximately $1.2 billion of cash from operations. This was driven by a robust earnings performance, coupled with an intentional inventory build to meet our growing customer demand. DSOs came in at 59 days, down from 68 days in Q2 due to the timing of customer shipments and invoicing. Our inventory turns dropped slightly from 1.7 in Q2 to 1.6 for the quarter.

We ended the quarter with $3.2 billion in inventory, up from $2.5 billion last quarter. Inventory level fluctuations are expected to continue as we work through the balancing of component timing and availability. This could result in quarters of elevated inventory balances affecting the timing of cash flow from operations ahead of customer deployments. Our purchase commitments at the end of the quarter were $11.4 billion, up from $9.7 billion at the end of Q2. As mentioned in prior quarters, this expected activity mostly represents purchases for chips related to new products and AI deployments. Our total deferred revenue balance was approximately $6.8 billion, down from $6.9 billion in the prior quarter.

The majority of the deferred revenue balance is product related. Our product deferred revenue decreased $86 million sequentially versus last quarter. We remain in a period of ramping our new products, winning new customers and expanding new use cases, including AI. These trends have resulted in increased customer-specific acceptance clauses and an increase in the volatility of our product deferred revenue balances. As mentioned in prior quarters, the deferred balance can move significantly on a quarterly basis, independent of underlying business drivers. Accounts payable days were 48 days, down from 57 days in Q2, reflecting the timing of inventory receipts and payments. Capital expenditures for the quarter were $100.7 million.

Our construction work to build expanded facilities in Santa Clara remains on track, and we expect construction to be completed in the coming months. As we look ahead, the momentum is strong. We are grateful to our customers and proud of our team's continuous ability to rise to meet the demands of the networking industry. For the fourth quarter, we are forecasting a range of revenue between $3.9 billion and $4 billion. This positions fiscal year 2026 revenue just over $13.3 billion at the midpoint. Our fourth quarter gross margin outlook is 63% to 64% and operating margin is between 48% and 49%.

Diluted EPS is forecasted to be between $1.26 and $1.30 with approximately 1.28 billion diluted shares, and the effective tax rate is expected to be approximately 21%. Looking further ahead to 2027, the momentum continues. For fiscal year 2027, the revenue growth outlook is between 38% and 40%, equating to approximately $18.5 billion at the midpoint. Gross margin continues to be in the range of 62% to 64% and an operating margin of approximately 49%. Our effective tax rate is expected to be approximately 21%. In closing, there is a lot to be excited about here at Arista. We will continue to be focused on our innovation, execution and delighting customers in the Arista way.

Rudolph Araujo:Thank you, Chantelle. We will now move to the Q&A portion of the Arista earnings call.[Operator Instructions]Regina, please take it away.

Operator:[Operator Instructions]Our first question comes from the line of Michael Ng with Goldman Sachs.

Michael Ng:I wanted to ask about your comment around the greater than 10 gigawatts of deployments across 10-plus compute accelerators for next year. Could you just talk a little bit about whether that is an industry number or an Arista-specific number in terms of those deployments? And how does the diversification of compute potentially create more opportunities for Arista networking relative to just having a handful of compute suppliers?

Jayshree Ullal:Thanks, Michael. As you know, I think much of AI, even in our world started initially being compute-centric, and we're seeing that change to network-centric. And so as part of the accelerated networking strategy, we are supporting 3 types of AI fabrics, scale-up, scale-out and scale-across. So our guess is by the end of '27, we will deploy largely in '26 and '27, is where the exponential ramp happened, across or greater than 10 gigawatts. Now some of that -- much of that gigawatt may be new. But remember, in scale-across, we can also have existing gigawatts being deployed. Operator:Our next question will come from the line of Meta Marshall with Morgan Stanley.

Meta Marshall:Congrats on the quarter. I guess just, Jayshree, if you could give an update just on how you see that mix of scale-across and scale-out and scale-up just as a mix of your business. Clearly, scale-up nothing today. I think last quarter, you had said you expected 1/3 of the demand this year to be from scale-across. Just as you've continued to increase your guidance and as you look into '27, just what do you see those mixes being?

Jayshree Ullal:I think in '27 -- Meta, thank you for the kind wishes. We've been working hard for this day. The scale-up will still be in early trials. So I don't think there's a material number associated with scale-up in '27. I do think it could contribute in '28. So then that -- if scale-up is virtually 0, then we're basically left with most of the use case being scale-out and scale-across. And as you've heard us say in the past, scale-across, we think, will be at least 1/3. It will probably go higher in '27. And so the split this year is roughly 70-30.

The split next year may be -- I can't venture to guess, but I think the 70 may come down and the 30 would go up when it comes to scale-across because it's a very strong use case for us. Arista is highly differentiated with our 7800 scale-across platform. And unsurprisingly, the word scale means a lot to us there and our customers, scale for security, scale for performance, scale for reliability, and there's just no room for error when you're connecting millions of XPUs. So we feel very comfortable that these are our 2 strongest use cases. I also think it will fuel -- I mean, a lot of this is back-end AI fabric.

We will come back to revisit a question of front end as well as we move to more inference and the line between back and front becomes thinner.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of Ben Reitzes with Melius Research.

Benjamin Reitzes:Jayshree, pretty good quarter guide there. So I just want -- you've previously referred to potentially 2 10%-plus customers into the fourth quarter. Do you mind talking about whether they're landing in that range and what the use cases are for and if you're excited about those customers still and into '27?

Jayshree Ullal:Yes. Yes, yes. So I guess diversity is the name of the game and the theme today, right, Chantelle?

Chantelle Breithaupt:That's right.

Jayshree Ullal:We have diverse accelerators. We have diverse models. We want to have diverse 10% customers, too. So as we said before, our dearest ones are M&M. We fully expect our top prior 10%-plus customers to continue to be with us in '26, and we hope beyond. And we expect to add at least 1, maybe 2. And a lot of that depends on whether Todd and Eugenia can ship enough product. So we'll let them decide, and we'll give them all the way into December 31.

Todd Nightingale:We'll take every day.

Jayshree Ullal:So we're feeling pretty good about at least 3 and maybe 4.

George Notter:I was just curious about the big sequential jump in R&D. It was really, really significant. I'm just wondering if that included some onetime items. Also, is this the new run rate in R&D going forward? Any perspective there would be great.

Jayshree Ullal:Okay. So over to you, Ken. Why did you spend so much money this year?

Kenneth Duda:We're building so much new stuff. The opportunity is humongous in AI, these AI accelerating systems are -- we are -- our success with the hyperscaler AI companies depends on our ability to partner. Our ability to partner is based on our understanding of each of their unique requirements and constraints. And also, there's a new technology introduction around liquid cooling. This requires major infrastructure upgrades and technology upgrades on our part. So I think that's what's really driving the expansion in spending there.

Chantelle Breithaupt:Sorry, George, just in your comment, is this new run rate, I'll still put the framework at anywhere between 9% and 11% as we work through. So some quarters like we've talked about, we'll hit this range as we have specific investments. And so I would still keep it in that 9% to 11%. More to come as we guide next year in more detail.

Jayshree Ullal:But I noticed the prototype bill was very high this quarter, Ken.

Kenneth Duda:That's right, because of all the opportunities in the hyperscaler AI space.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of Amit Daryanani with Evercore ISI.

Amit Daryanani:Congrats on a really good set of numbers over here. Jayshree, you talked initially about the industry moving towards a more network-centric architecture. As customers deploy different type of accelerators, does Arista become involved earlier in designing the overall systems rather than connecting them afterwards? And as you have to work with a more distributed disaggregated compute network, does that change your networking content per deployment? I know you talked about 10 gigawatts, I'm just sort of wondering, does the network intensity start to change as well?

And then maybe for Chantelle, as you think about this 38%, 40% guide for '27, which is extremely impressive, can you just touch on your confidence around the supply chain execution to meet this demand? What's in the bag versus what still needs to be closed?

Jayshree Ullal:Amit, this is a very good question. I think until now, we've enforced our architecture mostly on scale-out and scale-across. And a lot of that had to do with distributed power, location, moving to regional edges, a very software-defined type of network with the intensity, like I described, of package, flows, performance, predictable latency, et cetera. As we start participating with new accelerators, we get a greater chance early in the cycle to see the behavior of these accelerators. Two or 3 examples I'd like to highlight is our close work with Cerebras, our work with Microsoft and Maia.

These have been going on the last couple of years and has allowed us to tune our buffers, tune our software performance and maximize the I/O throughput, if you will. The recognition of those scale-up designs are still in the works, but they're already manifesting itself in scale-out and scale-across. So you bring up a very good point, not only in the actual work we're doing with these accelerators, but the aggregate impact it has on our network design in terms of scale, performance and reliability.

Chantelle Breithaupt:And then I think to part two of your question, Amit, and thank you for the kind words at the beginning, I think -- so I am confident in the guide, and I am confident in the supply chain. What makes me confident in the supply chain is internally, Todd and Eugenia and the team doing a fantastic job every day, being scrappy to make sure we can do what we need to do to deliver to our customers. And I also have confidence in a lot of great conversations and agreements with some of our key suppliers, and that's why you see our purchase commitments increasing because we have that confidence. So internally, externally confident.

As far as visibility, I think we have 2 quarters of visibility as we always have, and we lean into the other 2. But given our highly fungible portfolio, we're pretty clear where to make that bet. So we're pretty excited about next year.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of Tim Long with Barclays.

Timothy Long:Maybe if we could shift a little bit and talk about the campus and branch, pretty good year this year and guiding it to 60% next year. Could you talk a little bit about kind of what's enabling you to grow so much faster than the industry? And is this something that you see as a multiyear type of dynamic? Obviously, you got strength in enterprise data centers. But curious what else is helping this much higher than industry growth?

Todd Nightingale:Thanks for the question. In a lot of ways, I think the enterprise campus market is coming to us. Arista has always led the way in quality and reliability. And over the past few years, just practically every significant enterprise has shifted gears and really considered their campus networks, their branch networks mission-critical, with the highest need for reliability. This has only accelerated because of the Glasswing and Mythos effect where people are really focused deeply not only on providing the highest level of reliability, but being able to do that as they rapidly patch and adjust their infrastructure over time.

And the differentiation with EOS and the ability for Arista software to be able to do this with practically no downtime with extremely, extremely high uptime, it's highly differentiated in the market. And I really think that's the core of what's driving market share gains here.

Kenneth Duda:I think the other thing that makes this an incremental process is that campus refresh cycles are pretty long. So even customers that understand the Arista advantage may take some time to adopt us simply because of the schedule on which they depreciate and upgrade their gear. So I think we can expect this to be a multiyear cycle.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of David Vogt with UBS.

David Vogt:So maybe, Chantelle, one for you, and I'll wrap 2 together in 1 question. Can you kind of help us understand sort of your purchase commitment dynamic and your deferred revenue dynamic against the strong revenue guide that you provided for 2027? Chantelle Breithaupt:Thanks, David. I think there's a few things. Purchase commitments from that perspective, there are some things additionally we added and now we have memory in there, a memory agreement, which has done that. So that's a multiyear agreement that you'll see as the Q comes out. And I think on the purchase commitment side, you can probably expect that to go up a little bit more as we exit Q4, as we get ready for this 2027 guide we have.

As far as the deferred revenue, deferred revenue actually had the largest churn in and out and still remained flat and still delivered a 58.5% revenue growth quarter, which I think is a fantastic outcome. So there, you're seeing things exit again, released, and things to get booked back to the deferred balance, which I think is a really healthy sign of the demand that's fueling that 38% to 40% revenue growth next year. So I think they're all related. Purchase commitments grow to serve that demand and the deferred staying flat to deliver that outcome to the P&L. And we're pretty excited to see how that continues through 2027.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of Simon Leopold with Raymond James.

Simon Leopold:Appreciate that. I wanted to get one quick clarification. You gave us targets for 2027 for campus and AI. Just wanted to check on what the baselines are for 2026. And the question was really on a topic that I think Andy has been vocal about, but your thoughts about the evolution of switching with the inclusion of either CPO or NPO, what does that mean to Arista?

Jayshree Ullal:Okay. Just to clarify, the baseline upon our 38% to 40% is the '26 guide we gave of...

Chantelle Breithaupt:Yes, $13.3 billion.

Jayshree Ullal:$13.3 billion.

Chantelle Breithaupt:Yes. And within that, AI is $3.5 billion and campus is $1.25 billion.

Jayshree Ullal:Yes. We're staying with the target numbers because we only know actuals after we ship everything end of the year. And to your second question on optics, optics is very integral to Arista's strategy. Andy Bechtolsheim, our Chief Architect, lives and breathes this. It doesn't mean we build everything, but we actually systematically put it together. We, first of all, strongly believe in copper when you can and optics if you must, because the minute you go beyond the 1- or 2-meter radius, the flexibility of pluggable optics and lasers is probably the most widely deployed and accepted. Andy was a pioneer of OSFP that gave us a very wide density of thermal limits and widely used.

And now our new coherent optics, LPO modules is something that goes long distance without requiring DSP. And then to meet higher front panel density, we're very excited about extra-dense pluggable optics that can -- that is being supported by over 150 vendors. So we think the world is going to remain in a very majority fashion on pluggable optics. Having said that, I think there's always room for complementing the pluggables with a strong adoption at higher speeds to what we call near-packaged optics or open CPO. We don't want to build proprietary co-packaged optics.

And to solve these constraints, Arista has been pioneering this open CPO that instead of soldering components, we can use socketed optical engines and pigtail fibers to allow these modules to be pretested, et cetera. So we are big fans of these. We think they'll come on to the market in the '28 to '30 time frame. It's not imminent, but meanwhile, long live pluggable optics.

Joseph Cardoso:Congrats on the results as well. Maybe the question that I wanted to touch on and maybe it kind of dovetails off of the clarification on the last one. Jayshree Ullal:Thank you, Joe. Well, listen, when some things are growing 60% and 100%, and then you say the overall growth is 38% to 40%, then obviously, some of the things are not growing as fast, right? We're very comfortable that everything is going to grow double digits, some more, some less. And we're also very comfortable that given our first guide literally over a year before that all sectors are doing well for us, AI, enterprise, specialty cloud providers, front-end networks. So we started out 2026 wondering if front end would grow. So it's a cyclical thing. When the back end grows, the front end may grow a little slower.

When the back end slows down, the front end may grow a little faster. So I wouldn't read any conservatism into these numbers. These are wildly higher and optimistic than we had once projected. So enjoy them for a moment, and hopefully, they'll get better.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of James Fish with Piper Sandler.

James Fish:Fantastic quarter and guide here to start for '27, ladies, and Ken, of course.

Jayshree Ullal:We have 2 gentlemen and 2 ladies.

James Fish:And Todd, I don't -- I didn't forget about you, Todd. But look, I appreciate the early outlook, but you guys always talk about 1 to 2 quarters of visibility. You tend to be a very prudent team. And so maybe going back to, I think it was Amit's question, I guess, the confidence in providing the durability at this scale this early and why we're going to see this kind of strength persist, why Arista for scale-up in 2028?

Chantelle Breithaupt:Well, I'll just go back, and thank you for the kind words...

Jayshree Ullal:The kind words to the ladies and gentlemen.

Chantelle Breithaupt:That's right, to all of us. I think that -- so I'll just go back and reiterate the confidence level. There was a lot of thought, obviously, put into a guide this strong, this early. So there's a lot of attention paid with Todd and Ken and Jayshree and myself and team. So we had to get comfortable first, and we're very comfortable with all the things we've done to secure what we need to go ahead. And again, the 2 quarters visibility, 2 years of relationship and technical conversations, so somewhere between the second half lands, and it's the usual kind of cadence we have. So nothing's changed there.

I think from -- and then the second part of your question was about scale-up going into 2027, 2028. Jayshree?

Jayshree Ullal:Yes. So listen, I think scale-up has been a tough market for us because it doesn't have all the software advantages that we bring, but it absolutely has the hardware skills and all the non-NVIDIA accelerators that Arista is in the best position to connect to. So this movement from stand-alone basic switches to rack scale is something that Andy, Alex, Hugh Holbrook, the entire team has been working on and co-developing for a couple of years. It's hard work. Just as we were staring at InfiniBand and now we can go, of course, it's going to be Ethernet.

We're looking forward to a time where we were staring at proprietary UALink or NVLink, and we're going to go, of course, it's going to be ESUN. But these type of migrations are multiyear. And so we're very confident not only in our '27 guide, but a promising '28 ahead as well.
